name: fired-clay-figurines-venus
description: Hunter-gatherers baked moulded clay in a hearth, making the first known ceramic objects of any kind.

name: lime-plaster-burning
friendly_name: Lime Plaster Is Burned and Made
description: Builders heated limestone and mixed the result with water to make a hard white plaster for floors and walls.

name: first-copper-smelting-balkans
description: People learned to heat copper ore until it ran as liquid metal, making metal rather than just finding it.

name: varna-gold-grave-treasure
description: Craftsmen on the Black Sea coast hammered and shaped gold into hundreds of ornaments buried with their dead.

name: mesopotamian-kiln-fired-bricks
description: Builders along the great rivers began baking mud bricks in kilns, making walls that lasted far longer in damp.

name: bronze-alloyed-sumer
description: Smiths found that mixing tin into copper gave a tougher metal, and an entire age was named after it.

name: glass-made-mesopotamia
description: Craftsmen melted sand, soda and lime into the first man-made glass, shaped into beads and small vessels.

name: mesoamerican-rubber-curing
description: Peoples of the Gulf coast mixed latex with plant juice to make bouncing balls and waterproof items.

name: hittite-iron-mastery
description: Anatolian smiths began producing iron weapons and tools in quantity, ushering in a harder metal age.

name: roman-concrete-perfected
description: Builders mixed volcanic ash with lime and rubble to make a cement that set even underwater and still stands.

name: glassblowing-invented-syria
description: Craftsmen on the Syrian coast found molten glass could be inflated on a pipe, making vessels cheap and plentiful.

name: tang-true-porcelain
description: Kilns reached the heat needed to turn fine white clay into a hard, translucent ceramic prized worldwide.

name: murano-cristallo-glass
description: Venetian glassmakers found a way to make nearly colourless, clear glass fit to rival rock crystal.

name: bottger-european-porcelain
description: An alchemist in Saxony, ordered to make gold, instead worked out the secret of hard-paste porcelain.

name: darby-coke-smelting
description: An English ironmaster fuelled his blast furnace with coke instead of charcoal, making iron far cheaper.

name: parkesine-first-plastic
description: A British chemist showed off a mouldable material made from treated cellulose at a great exhibition.

name: polyethylene-discovered-icl
description: Chemists in an English lab found a waxy white solid in a high-pressure experiment, soon the commonest plastic.

name: synthetic-diamonds-ge
description: A General Electric team squeezed and heated graphite until it crystallised into diamond made by people.

name: pilkington-float-glass
description: An English firm floated molten glass on a bath of liquid tin, producing perfectly flat panes cheaply.
